I am 46 years old and have farmed these 8 mu in Quzhou County since I was a boy following my father around the fields. I never went to school, so everything I know comes from what I have seen with my own eyes and what my neighbors do. Last year my wheat gave me about 1000 jin per mu and my maize gave about 1100 jin — that is steady food for the family and some cash from selling the surplus. I am not touching cotton; my cousin grew it two years ago and spent the whole summer running back and forth spraying medicine, and then the price dropped at harvest and he barely broke even. No, I will stick to the wheat-maize rotation on all 8 mu, same as Lao Zhang next door and most everyone in the village.

For the wheat, I will rotary till before sowing in autumn and use improved seed like shimai. I will put down about two bags of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, and topdress with urea when the wheat greens up in spring. I know fertilizer costs money, but I would rather use a bit too much than too little — if the yield drops, I lose more than I save. I will irrigate three times: once before winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. For the maize, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest — the window is only a few days before the soil dries — so I will no-till sow hybrid seed like nongda372 straight into the wheat stubble. One bag of compound fertilizer at sowing is enough, and I will irrigate twice, at seedling stage and big trumpet stage. Four pesticide sprays on each crop keeps the weeds and bugs under control, which is what we have always done. I do not have money to gamble on new crops or fancy methods; a full belly and a stable income are what matter to me.
